chunks: Al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb narrated from Mālik ibn ʿAṭiyyah, from Sulaymān ibn Khālid, who said:

I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man whose father was a slave, and whose father had a wife who was a mukātabah and had already paid part of what she owed. The son of the slave said to her: "Would you like me to help you with your manumission contract so that you may pay what you owe, on condition that you will not have the option against my father when you gain ownership of yourself?" She said, "Yes." So he gave her for her manumission. Then: would she have the option after that?
He عليه السلام said: "She does not have the option. The Muslims are bound by their conditions."

key_terms.الْخِيَارُ: the legal option or right of choice
key_terms.شُرُوطِهِمْ: their stipulated conditions or contractual terms
key_terms.مَلَكْتِ نَفْسَكِ: you gained ownership of yourself, meaning you became free
key_terms.مَمْلُوكٌ: a slave; a person under ownership
key_terms.مُكَاتَبَةٌ: a bondwoman under a contractual arrangement to purchase her freedom

ai.seo_question: If a mukātabah woman agrees to a condition in exchange for help completing her manumission, is that condition binding after she becomes free?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a mukātabah woman who accepted financial help to complete her manumission in exchange for waiving her option regarding separation from her husband after gaining freedom. The Imam عليه السلام rules that she does not retain that option, affirming the legal principle that Muslims are bound by their conditions.
